market_holds: The Q3 2026 release is NOT pending at the close: Belite furnished it on a 6-K accepted 2026-11-12 11:05 UTC (06:05 ET), before today's open (EDGAR submissions; accession 0001104659-26-125573). Only the 4:30 pm ET conference call falls inside the window. Today's tape (Yahoo daily bars, read 19:19 UTC): opened 155.94 after a 155.94 close on 11-11, low 149.78, high 169.00, last 166.11 (+6.5%) on 346k shares against a ~164k 20-day average, so the stock has already reacted to the release on about twice normal volume. Baseline: 5-day run-up +15.26% (from the 143.19 close on 11-05), 20-day +8.14%, 14.8% under the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 56.6%, no usable option chain, and a median historical reaction of 2.91% that the baseline itself flags as unreliable (it is mostly 6-K operational updates). What the release held: FDA told the company it will NOT convene an advisory committee; NDA under priority review, PDUFA 2027-02-12; J-NDA filed under Sakigake; Access Consortium MAAs filed; cash $271.3m plus $502.7m in Treasuries (~$774m) at 2026-09-30; Q3 R&D $15.5m, SG&A $21.4m. view: This is a pre-revenue biotech with ~$774m of cash and a February 2027 PDUFA. The print's one market-moving line, confirmation that there will be no advisory committee, came out before the open and was traded all day: the stock is up ~6.5% at 166 on double volume. So the close-to-open window holds only the call, plus whatever analysts write overnight. For a company like this the call usually repeats the release: commercial readiness, PHOENIX interim timing (the release says only that an interim analysis is expected, with no date), label and pricing colour. Nothing found would make the call surprise in either direction. With $774m in the bank, a raise after the call is unlikely. A morning round of analyst notes on the no-AdCom news could lend mild support. Against that, the stock rose 15% in a week and 6.5% today into the call, so there is some fade risk. Neither side is supported by dated evidence strong enough to leave 50 by much.

recommendation.reason: The deciding information (no AdCom, PDUFA intact, cash) came out at 06:05 ET and the stock has spent a full session repricing it (+6.5%, ~2x volume). Only a call that usually repeats the release is left inside the window, and I found no mechanism that makes either side more likely than the price assumes.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A call disclosure not in the release: a firm, near-term PHOENIX interim readout date or a strong DSMB comment (up), or an FDA information request, a review extension, label or REMS concerns, or a financing announced after the call (down).

self_critique: Positive regulatory de-risking often drifts on as analysts publish overnight notes and price-target raises, which could lift tomorrow's open. Against that, a stock up 15% in a week and 6.5% today on news that was already guided could give some back before the open, especially if the call adds nothing. Either case is plausible and neither is evidenced well enough to act on.
approach_notes: P8 (stop early once you have shown the price holds the information) fit this name: the first EDGAR check showed the release came before the open. The playbook has no step to check whether the 'print' already happened before entry; a P1 line telling the researcher to confirm the release timestamp first would save time on names whose release and call straddle the close.
